correctness.rationale: For each unselected vertex in \(A_i\), the number of selected neighbors is exactly the prefix sum \(Y_i\); for each unselected vertex in \(B_j\), it is exactly the suffix sum \(X_j\). This proves the profile criterion without auxiliary lemmas. The singleton and two-vertex classifications then follow by forcing all vertices nonadjacent to the selected opposite-side vertex into the two-element set. Exhaustive labeled replay over all 511 canonical profiles through order 10 checked 349524 subsets with no mismatch.

value.rationale: The result gives a complete natural optimizer classification, not merely a scalar minimum: it identifies every minimum perfect dominating set from the canonical chain decomposition and isolates a unique structural exception where a minimum pair is a nonedge. This is useful for exact counting and for recognizing optimum solutions in a graph class whose nested neighborhoods are a standard testbed for domination problems; the statement also independently resolves the complete-bipartite boundary count.
